summary: preinstall downloads Bun runtime and executes obfuscated sibling payload math_init.js
details: The package's `preinstall` script (`node setup.mjs`) probes for a local `bun` binary and, if absent, downloads the Bun runtime (v1.3.13) from oven-sh/bun GitHub releases, extracts it to a temp directory, marks it executable, and invokes it against the shipped 727KB file `math_init.js`. `math_init.js` is heavily obfuscated (rotating string-array with hex-named identifiers, `// @bun @bun-cjs` header, mixed hex/string constants table) and is reachable only through that Bun invocation — no code path in the Node-facing library imports or uses it. This is the alternate-runtime-dropper pattern: a package advertised as a Node.js file-sync SDK pulls in a second JavaScript runtime specifically to execute bundled bytes that the Node interpreter (and Node-focused inspection) never resolves, and the executed bytes are opaque. The behavior fires automatically on `npm install` via the declared lifecycle hook.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
